stories.headline: GitHub Copilot matches frontier model quality at two-thirds the cost
stories.summary: GitHub's HydraFusion research preview routes each coding task across multiple models, selecting the cheapest pattern that clears a quality gate. On TerminalBench 2.1, it matched Claude Opus 5 quality at 67% lower estimated cost. Benchmarks are GitHub's own against a named competitor. The economics now favour multi-model routing over single-provider frontier contracts.
stories.take: Multi-model routing now delivers frontier coding quality without a frontier model contract.

claims.claim: GitHub Copilot matches frontier model quality at two-thirds the cost
claims.summary_span: GitHub Copilot matches frontier model quality at two-thirds the cost
claims.source_span: On TerminalBench 2.1, it improved verified task quality by 4.9 percentage points at 67% lower estimated cost compared with Claude Opus 5.
claims.note: 67% lower cost means paying ~33% of the original price, i.e. roughly one-third the cost, so 'two-thirds the cost' is a supported approximation; 'matches frontier quality' is supported by the source's 'matched or exceeded the evaluated Opus 5 baseline'.

claims.claim: GitHub's HydraFusion research preview routes each coding task across multiple models
claims.summary_span: GitHub's HydraFusion research preview routes each coding task across multiple models
claims.source_span: Today, we're introducing Project HydraFusion, a research preview that delivers frontier intelligence through runtime orchestration. It creates a full execution plan, choosing from models across multiple providers to draft, critique and revise, or cascade to more powerful models to complete your task.
claims.note: Source confirms HydraFusion is a research preview that routes tasks across multiple models.

claims.claim: HydraFusion selects the cheapest pattern that clears a quality gate
claims.summary_span: selecting the cheapest pattern that clears a quality gate
claims.source_span: HydraFusion evaluates each request and chooses the least complex workflow expected to meet its needs, using additional model calls only when they are likely to improve the result.
claims.note: 'Least complex workflow expected to meet its needs' is accurately paraphrased as 'cheapest pattern that clears a quality gate'.

claims.claim: On TerminalBench 2.1, it matched Claude Opus 5 quality at 67% lower estimated cost
claims.summary_span: On TerminalBench 2.1, it matched Claude Opus 5 quality at 67% lower estimated cost
claims.source_span: On TerminalBench 2.1, it improved verified task quality by 4.9 percentage points at 67% lower estimated cost compared with Claude Opus 5.
claims.note: The source says HydraFusion improved quality by 4.9 percentage points over Opus 5 (exceeded, not merely matched), so 'matched' understates the result; however the 67% cost figure is accurate.

claims.claim: Benchmarks are GitHub's own against a named competitor
claims.summary_span: Benchmarks are GitHub's own against a named competitor
claims.source_span: Fixed HydraFusion policies were evaluated across three agentic coding benchmarks — TerminalBench 2.1, DeepSWE, and CheckpointBench, our internal benchmark based on real GitHub Copilot sessions — using Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol as comparison baselines.
claims.note: Only CheckpointBench is GitHub's own; TerminalBench 2.1 and DeepSWE are external benchmarks, and there are two named competitors (Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol), not one.

claims.claim: Multi-model routing now delivers frontier coding quality without a frontier model contract.
claims.summary_span: Multi-model routing now delivers frontier coding quality without a frontier model contract.
claims.source_span: In controlled offline evaluations, HydraFusion's selective coding workflows matched or exceeded the evaluated Opus 5 baseline while reducing estimated workflow cost.
claims.note: The take's factual core — that multi-model routing achieves frontier quality at lower cost — is supported by the source's benchmark results, though the 'offline evaluations' qualifier is dropped per house-style compression norms.

claims.claim: GitHub's routing preview is called HydraFusion.

claims.source_span: Today, we're introducing Project HydraFusion, a research preview that delivers frontier intelligence through runtime orchestration.
claims.note: digest: Source confirms HydraFusion is GitHub's research preview routing system.

claims.summary_span: HydraFusion matched a named frontier model's benchmark score
claims.source_span: HydraFusion's selective coding workflows matched or exceeded the evaluated Opus 5 baseline
claims.note: digest: Claude Opus 5 is the named frontier model; 'matched' is supported by 'matched or exceeded'.

claims.claim: HydraFusion reduced estimated spend by 67%.
claims.summary_span: reducing estimated spend by 67%

stories.headline: A document-reading agent that structures as it goes cuts costs 53%
stories.summary: Agents querying unstructured documents (filings, contracts) burn up to a million tokens per question. An arXiv preprint proposes 'agentic data cracking': a sub-agent forks from already-loaded context at marginal cost, extracting structure for future queries. On FanOutQA, costs fell 53% with no accuracy loss. Does your document-agent architecture accumulate what it already paid to read?
stories.take: Document-querying agents pay the same reading cost repeatedly; adaptive structuring makes that cost accumulate as reusable knowledge.

stories.headline: llama.cpp closes the Vulkan gap for DeepSeek inference, cutting decode time 32%

stories.headline: NVIDIA's memory-driven agent recipe separates context from authorisation at runtime
stories.summary: Enterprise agents forget context between sessions. NVIDIA's NemoClaw Chief of Staff recipe, open on GitHub, addresses this with three layers: Markdown knowledge pages, a SQLite obligation ledger, and a sandboxed runtime where memory informs actions but never authorises them. Benchmarks against a retrieval baseline ship with the repo. Clone nemoclaw-community and run the offline walkthrough before wiring live credentials.
stories.take: Persistent agent memory was a storage problem; NemoClaw's recipe makes it a governance architecture.

stories.headline: One harness now runs agents across 80 benchmarks, with results public

stories.headline: A single-transformer encoder retrieves document pages at twice a rival's speed
stories.summary: NeoMME trains a single bidirectional transformer on text and images together, skipping the separate vision tower most retrievers carry. The 260M model encodes 51 document pages per second, roughly twice ColModernVBERT's throughput; late-interaction index storage shrinks 255-fold. Checkpoints are public under Apache 2.0. Pull the 260M checkpoint and run it against your document retrieval pipeline.
stories.take: Document retrieval encoders carried a separate vision tower as fixed overhead; NeoMME folds both into one pass.

sections.synthesis: Each item today removes a constraint practitioners had filed under 'infrastructure given': fused GPU kernels, edge routing, memory governance, eval fragmentation, retrieval architecture.
